world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.source_named: Zielenbach 2026 'Half silver, half gold: Modole folk stories and a first sketch grammar' (LangSci OTC 6) downloaded and searched in full: no stress/accent statement anywhere in the sketch.

new_statements.quote: Ik merk nog op dat, hoewel geschreven heel veel overeenkomst is tusschen deze talen, gesproken heel veel verschil bestaat. In de eerste plaats draagt daartoe bij het verschillend leggen van den klemtoon. Het Galéla b.v.b. verandert den klemtoon nooit door toevoeging van achtervoegsels, het Tobèlo brengt den klemtoon juist op het achtervoegsel over; het Madole spreekt de exponenten o, ma, etc. uit, alsof deze een integrerend deel van het woord zijn en geeft die den klemtoon, enz. Op het gehoor is tusschen deze talen heel wat verschil, zoodat men elkaar over en weer niet verstaat.
new_statements.translation: I note further that, although in writing there is a great deal of agreement between these languages, in speech there is a great deal of difference. In the first place the different placement of the stress contributes to this. Galela, for example, never changes the stress by the addition of suffixes; Tobelo shifts the stress precisely onto the suffix; Madole pronounces the exponents o, ma, etc. as if they were an integral part of the word and gives them the stress, etc. By ear there is a considerable difference between these languages, so that they do not understand one another.
new_statements.citation: Hueting, A. 1908. Iets over de "Ternataansch-Halmahèrasche" taalgroep. Bijdragen tot de Taal-, Land- en Volkenkunde van Nederlandsch-Indië 60: 369-411 (DOI 10.1163/22134379-90001928), p. 409.
new_statements.locator: p. 409, concluding section ('Slot-beschouwing'), second paragraph; archive.org scan dli.ministry.10280, leaf 473 = PDF page 474
new_statements.check: confirmed by a second reader, with minor differences
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Quote check: opened lines 31624-31637 and the page image pages/running head 'IETS OVER DE TERNATAANSCH-HALMAHERASCHE TAALGROEP. 409'). The passage is there as quoted, in the second paragraph of p. 409 inside the 'Slot-beschouwing'. Minor differences only: the print reads 'Galèla' (grave), the quote has 'Galéla'; 'Madole' and 'die' are letter-spaced for emphasis in print (the emphasis on 'die' = 'gives THOSE the stress'); the scanned's stray comma after 'klemtoon' before 'juist' is not in the print and the quote correctly omits it. Otherwise verbatim: '... het Madole spreekt de exponenten o, ma, etc. uit, alsof deze een integrerend deel van het woord zijn en geeft die den klemtoon, enz.' Rea…
new_statements.rule_in_words: The only first-hand remark on Modole stress: the proclitic 'exponents' o and ma (Zielenbach 2026's noun marker and relational noun marker) are pronounced as part of the following word and take the stress. Hueting never states the default position of stress within a Modole root (his Galela/Tobelo comparanda imply a root-based stress that suffixes may or may not shift, but he gives no position); so no placement rule (penult etc.) can be read from this source.
new_statements.exceptions: None; the remark ends with 'enz.' (etc.), i.e. it is an illustrative, not exhaustive, comparison.
new_statements.domain_note: Phonological word including proclitic noun markers, in connected speech; a comparative aside by the Tobelo missionary (self-described 'leek op taalgebied'), not a phonological description. Language name given as Madole; no dialect specified.
new_statements.identity_note: Hueting 1908 writes 'Madole' (= Modole, modo1249; Zielenbach 2026: 15 and Voorhoeve 1988 confirm the spelling variant). His remark is about the language as a whole; Ellen's 1916 material reflects the northern (h-) dialect per Zielenbach 2026 citing Voorhoeve 1988. Not to be confused with Pagu (pagu1249) or Tobelo (tobe1251), the comparanda in the same sentence.

sources.note: p. 409 (concluding 'Slot-beschouwing'): spoken differences between the group's languages come 'in the first place' from different placement of stress; Galela never shifts stress under suffixation, Tobelo shifts it onto the suffix, and 'het Madole spreekt de exponenten o, ma, etc. uit, alsof deze een integrerend deel van het woord zijn en geeft die den klemtoon'. No default stress position for Modole is stated; no other klemtoon remark in the article (grep of the article range). Verified against the page image.

sources.citation: Zielenbach, Maria. 2026. Half silver, half gold: Modole folk stories and a first sketch grammar (Open Text Collections 6). Berlin: Language Science Press. DOI 10.5281/zenodo.17511782.
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 5.2 'Orthography' (pp. 28-31) is explicitly limited to 'basic phonology issues that can be gathered from the written text alone' (consonant/vowel inventories, glottal stop, u>o sandhi); the sketch is corpus-based on Ellen's 1916 texts. Full-text grep: 0 hits for stress/accent/prosod/penult/intonation/pitch. Confirms the earlier scan verdict.

sources.citation: Wada, Yuiti. 1980. Correspondence of consonants in North Halmahera languages and the conservation of archaic sounds in Galela. Senri Ethnological Studies 7: 497-529.
sources.note: Comparative consonant study with a 229-item Modole wordlist (two speakers, 1976). Only accent remark is about Galela ('the final syllable is preserved even in Galela when the accent falls on the penultimate', p. 509); nothing on Modole stress.

sources.citation: Ellen, G. J. 1916a. Woordenlijst van het Modòle op Noord-Halmahera, bevattende slechts de van het Tobeloreesch afwijkende woorden. Bijdragen tot de Taal-, Land- en Volkenkunde 72: 103-139. DOI 10.1163/22134379-90001694.
sources.note: Nothing. The one-page Inleiding (p. 103, read on the page image) notes only that Modole lacks k and has a glottal stop (hamzah, written ') in its place, and that the spelling follows Van Baarda and Hueting. Entries occasionally carry accent marks (scanned shows ~40 é/ê in ~1,000 entries, e.g. 'Modòle', 'hélero') but their function is never stated; Zielenbach 2026 also calls Ellen's diacritics unexplained.
